messages:
anya: Heads-up — saw a steady memory climb on canary after the new kernel selector + batching heuristic landed. Long streaming chats with tool loops hit +2.3GB over 2 hours on a 16GB pod.

mike: Which canary? link to the deploy?

deploy-bot: rolled out canary: infra/canary/2026-03-17T21:10Z -> kernel-selector:v3 + batching:adaptive-v2

anya: Yep that one. Repro steps: start a ~30min streaming chat w/ repeated toolcall loops (~200 tool calls, each short). Memory graph shows monotonic growth, not stepy. No OOM, just paging pressure.

sanjay: Can you paste top of pmap or heap profile?

anya: quick pmap snapshot:
```
00000000 kB rw-p  2,356,736  heap
00000000 kB rw-p    128,000  kv_cache_pages
00000000 kB rw-p  1,048,576  batch_buffer
```

anya: heap profile (abridged):
```
  44%  runtime  kv_page_slot_alloc
  23%  runtime  pending_prefetch_entries
  12%  user     batching_window_buffers
```

lucy: interesting — "pending_prefetch_entries" jumped after kernel v3 selected dynamic-shared kernel for context lengths > 1024. Might be prefetch policy being too eager and pinning pages.

ryan: also check eviction: our eviction treadmill runs every 5s, but adaptive batching extends KV residency window to avoid misses. Could be they interact to prevent reclaim.

mike: Can we repro with a smaller test? e.g. 5 tool loops with artificial long context?

anya: I built a local harness that simulates repeated tool loops and streaming tokens. Command: `./stress_longchat --loops 200 --ctx 4096 --tool-lat 20ms`. Repro reliably in ~30 min.

sanjay: Added perf counters while running: major page faults and anon_hugemap growth correlated with number of prefetches. Stack traces point to kv_prefetcher::fetch_range -> kv_page_pin -> allocator::hold_slot.

lucy: Can you try disabling prefetcher (flag kv.prefetch=false) and re-run? If memory stabilizes, we know prefetch policy is culprit.

anya: Ran that. With kv.prefetch=false the growth flattened, memory stayed ~stable after warmup. With prefetch on it kept climbing.

ryan: So hypothesis: prefetch policy + adaptive batching increases in-flight ranges; eviction sweeper fails to evict because pages are pinned via prefetcher and batch buffers. Could be an epoch race where prefetch pins survive sweep boundary.

mike: Code paths to inspect: kernel-selector's hinting that sets `kernel_hint = dynamic_shared` triggers larger batch aggregation. That bumps `batch_window_ms` and we found a regression where `pin_lifetime` defaults to 10s instead of 1s for aggregated batches.

anya: Found the line: in batching_adaptive.cpp we set `pin_lifetime = batch_window_ms * 1.0` in the canary. Should be min(batch_window_ms, DEFAULT_PIN_MS). Oops.

lucy: Nice catch. So the quick fix is clamp pin_lifetime. But we should also add an eviction predicate that ignores prefetch pins older than X and lets sweeper reclaim if under memory pressure.

mike: Agreed. I'll open a PR with the clamp and an additional metric to track pinned-by-prefetch timestamps. Also add an e2e test that runs the harness for 1h and asserts memory delta < 200MB.

anya: Filing bug: #INF-1843. Patch + test should go to canary branch. For rollbacks: we can flip `batching:adaptive-v2` -> adaptive-v1 or disable kernel dynamic hint until fixed.

deploy-bot: created ticket INF-1843 and linked to PR draft 4321.

ryan: Nits — add a Prometheus gauge `kv_prefetch_pinned_count` and a histogram for pin_age_seconds. That will save us from chasing similar issues.

anya: Will add metrics. For now rolling back batching heuristic on canary to adaptive-v1 and disabling kernel hint. I’ll post a short summary in #eng-runtime when done.

mike: Thanks everyone. Great triage. :thumbsup:
